title: A writer or reviewer session starts with the task's skills already loaded
description: Diagnosis (stage 1 a1d-a4d, 2026-10-23): neither the writer prompt nor the plain prompt routes skills; in both arms the only thing that leads a session to the Skill tool is the superpowers SessionStart text, and the model takes that choice on its first turn or never - a1d/a2d and a3d/a4d had byte-identical prompts and session starts and split one-and-one. Probed on CLI 2.1.307: `--agents <file> --agent <name>` with a `skills` field does NOT preload the skill in -p main-session mode (the session answered NONE, as the control did); `--append-system-prompt <SKILL.md text>` does (the session quoted the skill's token with no tool call). _areas.resolve_skills already resolves a task's skills (area defaults, then the task's) for the executor brief, but run-agent-session never uses it, and this plan declares no area and no task skills.
desiredOutcome: Every writer and reviewer session the drive starts has the full text of each skill the task resolves to in its context from the first turn, recorded by name and digest in the session's record, and a plan can name house skills once for every phase; a named skill the launcher cannot find stops the launch by name

findings.issue: Unverified: the reviewer's skills are appended with --append-system-prompt-file ALONGSIDE --agents/--agent audit-reviewer, but the only live probe the phase cites (claude 2.1.307) was main-session mode without --agent. The executor states no live check was made (fake claude only). Nothing handed shows that, under --agent, the appended file still reaches the session's system prompt rather than being replaced by the agent's prompt. ras45 pins only that the argv carries both flags and that the stub saw the file, so it would pass even if claude ignored the append for an agent session. The phase's desired outcome ('every writer AND reviewer session ... from the first turn') rests on this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.4-myr (c3ebab8a6c3b): Before sign-off, run one cheap real reviewer-role session (--agent audit-reviewer plus --append-system-prompt-file holding a sentinel) and record that the session quotes the sentinel with no Skill call; if it does not, append the skills to the --agents definition's prompt for the reviewer instead. Record the probe command and result in the task or the guide paragraph.

findings.issue: The resolution order is project, then user, then plugin, and ras35 asserts that the project copy of a name the user also has wins. As I recall Claude Code's documented precedence for same-named skills it is enterprise, then personal (<outside-repo>), then project, with plugin skills namespaced as plugin:skill only; I did not verify this (no network, no live session), so treat it as a question the task should settle. If I recall correctly, a same-named project and user skill would be preloaded from the project while the session's own Skill tool would load the user's, i.e. two different bodies for one name. The task description states the project-first order, so this is not a contradiction of the clause; it is the clause possibly resting on a wrong premise, and a test now pins it. Also, a bare name is looked up in the plugin's skills/, whereas a session sees plugin skills only as plugin:skill.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.4-myr (c3ebab8a6c3b): Check the order against the Claude Code skills documentation (verifying-external-behavior) and, if personal outranks project, swap the two entries in skill_places and the order in ras35/ras43 and the guide paragraph; if project outranks user, cite the source in the skill_places docstring.

findings.issue: skills_prompt wraps the SKILL.md text as <skill name=...> but never says where the skill lives. A skill that points at sibling files gets no base directory: .claude/skills/before-you-claim/SKILL.md:117 names `references/questions.md`, and before-you-claim is one of the three Python house skills this repo's plan means to preload. The Skill tool would give the session the directory; this path does not, so the reference cannot be followed.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.4-myr (c3ebab8a6c3b): Put the skill's directory in the wrapper (e.g. <skill name="..." dir="...">) and add a case that the attribute is the SKILL.md's folder.

findings.issue: A second resolver of 'where does this plan-named skill live': audit:doctor's check_plan_skills (status/_doctor_policy.py:385) discovers skills through installed plugins as well, while skill_places knows three places and refuses any plugin:skill whose plugin is not the running one. A plan naming an installed third-party skill (e.g. superpowers:...) that doctor reports as resolving makes the drive refuse the launch at run time, with no way out except task.skills null. The refusal is what the clause asked for; the divergence between the two resolvers and the lack of a pre-launch signal is the cost.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.4-myr (c3ebab8a6c3b): Either say in the refusal message that only the project, the user's directory and this plugin are searched (and that skills: null opts out), or have doctor's check use skill_places so the two agree; consider running find_skills in the drive before starting the task so the refusal comes before the task is marked in_progress.

findings.issue: The verb advertises a manifest positional (usage block `default-skills (--skills a,b [--replace] | --remove) [manifest]`; verbs-in-full.md `[<manifestPath>]`) but never calls `_manifest_from_positional(args)` as `cmd_reindex` (and the other id-less verbs) does. The path lands in `args.title` and is silently ignored, so the plan written is the one resolved from --project-dir / CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / cwd, not the one named. Checked by running both verbs against a scratch repo with a nonexistent manifest path: `reindex /nonexistent/zzz.json` exits 2 with 'manifest not found: /nonexistent/zzz.json', while `default-skills --remove /nonexistent/zzz.json` ignores the path and answers about the scratch repo's own plan. A caller who names plan X and gets plan Y written is the lock/journal/manifest split the helper's own docstring warns of. No case passes a manifest positional, so dsv1/dsv2 cannot see it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.3-myr (9cab033e908e): Call `_manifest_from_positional(args)` first in cmd_default_skills, before `_resolve_project`, and add a dsv case that passes the plan path as the positional with a different --project-dir and asserts the named plan changed and a nonexistent path is refused by name.

The diff declares nothing; the executor's outcome says 'Not done by this task ... a post-merge step with the verb'. The clause was in the description and the phase outcome ('a plan can name house skills once') is not exercised for this repo until it is done, so the intent is not met as written. The narrowed scope is the executor's own, not the description's.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.3-myr (9cab033e908e): Run `audit-task.py default-skills --skills writing-python,before-you-claim,no-silent-pass --reason ...` against the plan from the merged code (or file a dedicated follow-up task for it before P138 signs off) and record it, rather than leaving it as a prose note.

findings.issue: Three statements of the resolution order still describe two levels. manifest-conventions.md says executor skills are 'each tag's skills first, then task.skills ... area first' (a file the executor/orchestrator reads, and the one the area section points to as the rule); the executor brief prints 'No skill resolves for this task: no area default and no task skill.'; the unresolved-skills warning offers only 'set task.skills, register default skills on an area, or write null' and `_skills_in_use` ignores a plan that wrote only meta.defaultSkills. Each now omits the new first level.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.3-myr (9cab033e908e): Update the conventions bullet to 'meta.defaultSkills, then each tag's skills, then task.skills'; say 'no plan default, no area default and no task skill' in the brief; add 'set meta.defaultSkills with audit-task.py default-skills' to the warning's exits.

findings.issue: P138-R7 is fixed for one of its three statements only. Its resolution reads 'say "no plan default, no area default and no task skill" in the brief; add "set meta.defaultSkills with audit-task.py default-skills" to the warning's exits'. The diff changes the conventions bullet and a comment at audit-lookup.py:139, but the brief line still reads 'No skill resolves for this task: no area default and no task skill.' and the unresolved-skills warning still offers only 'set task.skills, register default skills on an area in meta.areas, or write "skills": null'. The outcome says '_manifest_typos.py ... untouched and still correct', but the warning's exit list omits the plan-level exit the phase introduced. _skills_in_use (_manifest_typos.py:178-195) also does not count meta.defaultSkills as use.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.7 (04261ee5efac): Reword the brief line to name the plan default, add the meta.defaultSkills exit to the warning (and its test__manifest_typos case), or record in the outcome that those two are deliberately left and why.

findings.issue: P138-R5's resolution asks for a case that 'asserts the named plan changed and a nonexistent path is refused by name'. dsv3 covers the first half and the call order, not the nonexistent-path half. I ran `default-skills --remove /nonexistent/zzz.json` outside any plan with the fixed code: exit 2, '[audit-task] not a directory: /nonexistent', so the behaviour holds, but nothing pins it. The refusal names the root, not the manifest path.

findings.issue: co1, the case that pins the R7 conventions bullet, lives in tests/test_audit_lookup.py, but the task's tests.gate is only `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_task.py`. The recorded gate run (passed) therefore never ran co1. The executor ran test_audit_lookup.py by hand (143/143) but no recorded gate did.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.7 (04261ee5efac): Add tests/test_audit_lookup.py to the task's gate set (retarget --gate-set) so the run that records the evidence also runs co1.

findings.issue: The two callers still disagree for one class of name, so the stated purpose ('Two answers is how doctor goes green over a name the launcher then refuses', PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md _skill_places section) is only half met. check_plan_skills passes `inventory=` built from `_panel_discovery.discover`, whose scan walks every installed plugin's skills/ (`_plugin_bases`, `_scan_skills(base, 'plugin', ...)`) under bare keys. A bare name that is only some other installed plugin's skill therefore resolves in doctor (source 'scan') and is refused by `run-agent-session` (no inventory), which is the exact green-then-refused shape the task set out to remove. dp52 cannot see it: its inventory (`others`) holds only 'unrelated' and 'scan-only', and neither is in the dp52 name list; dp50 locks the wider mode as 'what doctor saw before'.
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.5-myr (d1e8d9948576): Either drop the inventory mode for bare names the session would not load, or keep it but say so: when `resolve_skill` returns source 'scan', have doctor word the row as 'found only by the machine scan at <path>; `run-agent-session --skill` will refuse it', and add a dp52 name that only the inventory lists, asserting doctor and the launcher answers differ visibly rather than silently.

findings.issue: The diff reverses the launcher's order to personal-before-project, but the portability grade in `_plan_skills_travel` is still read from `have.get(name)`, the scan entry, and the scan dedupes project before user ('project/user scanned before plugins win', `_discover_scan` scans `.claude` of the project first). For a name held by both, doctor's resolved path is now the personal copy while `travels`/`travelsBasis` describe the project copy: a plan can be graded 'travels' over a file the session does not load. The executor names this in the outcome and leaves it for another task, but it is created by this change (before it, launcher and scan agreed on project-first).
findings.resolution: fixed in P138.5-myr (d1e8d9948576): In `_plan_skills_travel`, compare `entry.get('path')` with `resolved[name]['path']` and, when they differ, put the name in `unknown` with both paths named (the grade belongs to a different file than the one loaded), or make the scan's project/user order match `_skill_places`. Add a dp case with the same name in both tiers.

findings.issue: The note that `claude --help` does not list `--append-system-prompt-file`, with the probe's build and date, sits in the module docstring (line 35). The only place the flag is written in code (`session_argv`, line 217) carries no comment, and ras50 reads 700 characters around the FIRST occurrence of the string only, which is the docstring. The task asked for it 'beside the flag'.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.2 (d5cce403c68f): Add a one-line comment above `argv += ["--append-system-prompt-file", skills_file]` pointing at the docstring probe (claude 2.1.307, 2026-10-23), and have ras50 check the last occurrence as well.

findings.issue: Three comments still describe the removed mode. run-agent-session.py:249 says 'and no inventory is passed, so only a SKILL.md this launcher can read counts' (the parameter no longer exists); test__doctor_policy.py:458 says 'The scan inventory stays the WIDER mode: a name only the scan lists still resolves here' directly above dp50, which now asserts the opposite; test__skill_places.py:92 is headed 'the scan inventory is the wider mode' over cases that assert there is none. A sentence claiming what the code does not do.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.2 (d5cce403c68f): Reword the three: the launcher and doctor ask the same resolver and there is no inventory argument; drop 'WIDER' from the dp comment and retitle the sp section 'no second mode'.

findings.issue: _scan_sighting words every scan-listed refusal as 'which a session does not load by that bare name'. The scan keys a skill by its front-matter name (_panel_discovery.py:137 `fm.get('name') or name`) while the resolver looks for a directory of that name. So a skill under <home>/skills/<dir>/SKILL.md with `name: other` is listed as 'other' at a path in a directory the launcher DOES read, and the row says a session does not load it, with no hint that the cause is the directory/name mismatch. The docstring's two causes ('another plugin's skill, or a copy in a place no session reads') omit this third one. The refusal itself is consistent with the launcher; the explanation can mislead.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.7 (04261ee5efac): When the sighting path sits under one of resolved[name]['places']' skills directories, say the directory name differs from the skill's front-matter name (the launcher looks up the directory name); add the case next to dp53.

findings.issue: R13 is closed in doctor only. The executor's descriptive outcome says 'a portability grade only counts when it describes the file a session loads', but _panel_write.py:2130 (the strict-tier refusal of a patched skill name) still reads `have.get(name).get('travels')` from the scan entry, which for a name in both tiers is the project copy while the launcher loads the personal one. audit-status.py:279 has the same shape but asks the repo-scope clone question, where the project copy is arguably the right one. The R13 finding named only _plan_skills_travel, so this is outside what was asked; it is the same class and the claim overreaches.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.7 (04261ee5efac): Narrow the descriptive outcome to doctor, and file the strict-tier refusal in _panel_write.py as a follow-up (compare the entry path with the resolved path there too, or resolve through _skill_places).

tasks.title: run-agent-session preloads the task's resolved skills into the session's system prompt and records them
tasks.description: Give run-agent-session.py a repeatable --skill NAME (the drive passes _areas.resolve_skills(manifest, phase, task) for both the writer and the reviewer). For each name, locate SKILL.md the way Claude Code resolves a skill for a session in that tree - the project's .claude/skills/<name>/, the user's <outside-repo><name>/, then the running plugin's own skills/ (a plugin-qualified name plugin:skill only from that plugin) - and refuse to start, exit E_USAGE with the name and every place looked, when one is missing: a declared skill that does not load is the defect this phase exists for. Write the bodies, each wrapped with its name, to one file under the session's scratch and pass it as --append-system-prompt-file (keep the task prompt on stdin byte-identical). Record in the session's record line the preloaded names, paths and sha256 of each body, so a reader can tell which skills a session had without a Skill call. The reviewer keeps its --agents body; the skills append to it the same way. Cases: the argv carries the file when skills resolve and carries no such flag when none do; the file holds each body once in resolution order; a missing skill refuses with its name; the record names each skill with its digest; the prompt on stdin is unchanged.

A missing name -> refuse() -> E_USAGE naming the skill and every path looked in; an existing but undecodable/unreadable SKILL.md -> io-error, E_IO. load_skills reads bytes, sha256 of the file bytes; skills_prompt wraps each full SKILL.md as <skill name=...>...</skill>; _prepare writes one <stream>.skills.md under the scratch; session_argv adds --append-system-prompt-file only when skills were named (before --agents, so the resume pair stays last and ras17 still holds). write_record gains a skills list (name, path, sha256) only when skills were named; _run takes an out-dict `ran` so the record carries them whichever outcome follows. (ws*, rv*, sr2) still pass in the full run. tasks.title: A plan names house skills once, and every phase's tasks resolve them
tasks.description: Today a skill reaches a task only through a registered area the phase names, or the task's own list, so a plan whose phases carry no area (this one) resolves nothing. Add a plan-wide default - an existing mechanism if _areas already has one, else a new meta key read first by resolve_skills, before area defaults and the task's own (adding a key is free under COMPATIBILITY.md; document it there and in the schema and audit-config docs as appropriate) - with task.skills null still opting out. Declare this repository's Python house skills there through the plugin's own verb (no hand edit of docs/audit): writing-python, before-you-claim, no-silent-pass. Cases: a phase with no area resolves the plan default; area and task skills follow it, deduped; null opts out; the validator accepts the key and rejects a non-list.
